transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. It's nice to meet you too. 

Well, I'm here because I've realized I keep arranging my own house around not seeing spiders. It's getting to be too much. I put off doing laundry because the machines are in the basement, and I completely avoid the garden shed. I'm even paying people to do small jobs around the house that I know perfectly well how to do myself, simply because I can't make myself go into those spaces.
When you think about going into those places, is it specifically the possibility of encountering a spider that scares you?

Yes, exactly. I mean, logically, I know a spider hanging out in the corner of an old house probably isn’t going to actually hurt me. But... the moment I even just picture one dropping out of a storage box, or sitting there near the washer, it just feels enormous. It becomes this incredibly threatening thing in a way that I’m honestly pretty embarrassed to admit.
If you do come across a spider, do you get a sudden rush of intense fear or panic right away?

Yes, absolutely. If I actually spot one, my chest tightens up right away. My hands start shaking, and I just... I either completely freeze in the doorway or I back out of the room so fast. It's almost like my body has decided to run away before my brain even has time to process what's happening.
